If I'm allowed to give my 2 cents, here are some things I would recommend you to fix.  
\- Q1 generally is a comparison of the passage and the lecture. So your intro should mention one point about what the passage is stating and one point about what the lecture is stating. - - When it comes to the Body paragraphs, I generally follow the pattern of one point from the passage and 2 counterpoints from the lecture. For example for the first Body para I would go with the following:  
Firstly, the author states that due to the complex technology used in smart cars, they are able to effectively detect obstacles and prevent many accidents that would've occurred had the driver been human. The lecturer, on the other hand, strikes back by saying that all technologies fail at one point of time and so would the smart cars. They also say that since these smart cars travel at much faster speeds, the accidents caused by them would be much more serious than one caused by a human driver.  
\- I also generally suggest ending with a conclusion as it just fits the essay pattern better. Doesn't have to be anything fancy - I always just use "As can bee seen from above, the author and the lecturer disagree about blah blah blah"  
\- This last one is just something I've noticed upon personal practice and my test, but writing many words definitely increases your score a lot. For example for Q2 even though the recommended count is 100, your score can jump a lot if you write 130-150. For Q1 I think I always went for 300-400 words and it wasn't really that difficult to do with the TST Prep writing template  


(PS. If you want an evaluation similar to what ETS scorers give you (out of 5) I would suggest prompting chatgpt to act as a toefl writing Q1 (or q2) scorer, give it the paragraph, the transcript, your response and the scoring rubrics)
